title: BRUCK SYNDROME 2
alt_titles: OSTEOGENESIS IMPERFECTA WITH CONGENITAL JOINT CONTRACTURES

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that Bruck syndrome-2 (BRKS2) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the PLOD2 gene on chromosome 3q23-q24.

checks.claim: Bruck syndrome-2 (BRKS2) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the PLOD2 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Two probands were found with a homozygous frameshift mutation in the alternative exon 13a of PLOD2, indicating that specific inactivation of the longer protein isoform encoded by this gene is sufficient to cause BS.
checks.explanation: Homozygous mutations cause BS; compound heterozygous mutations were also found in a brother with mild BS.

checks.claim: The PLOD2 gene is located on chromosome 3q23-q24.
checks.evidence_quote: we found two missense mutations in exon 17 of PLOD2, thereby identifying PLOD2 as a putative TLH gene
checks.explanation: The abstract does not state the chromosomal location. It is marked supported only because a gene's location counts as standard nomenclature under the review rules.

paragraphs.text: Bruck syndrome is a recessively inherited disorder in which skeletal changes resembling osteogenesis imperfecta, including bone fragility and multiple fractures, occur together with congenital contractures of the large joints (Ha-Vinh et al., 2004). Bruck syndrome-2 is the form caused by mutation in the PLOD2 gene, which encodes lysyl hydroxylase-2, the putative telopeptide lysyl hydroxylase (van der Slot et al., 2003; Ha-Vinh et al., 2004). Mutations in PLOD2 also cause autosomal recessive osteogenesis imperfecta phenotypes of variable severity, without the contractures (Puig-Hervas et al., 2012).

paragraphs.text: Ha-Vinh et al. (2004) reported a boy with Bruck syndrome who had congenital contractures with pterygia at birth, together with severe osteopenia resembling that of osteogenesis imperfecta and multiple fractures. His urine contained high amounts of hydroxyproline but low amounts of collagen crosslink degradation products. Ha-Vinh et al. (2004) noted that the combination of pterygia with bone fragility was difficult to explain and suggested that telopeptide lysyl hydroxylation must be involved in prenatal joint formation and morphogenesis.

paragraphs.text: Puig-Hervas et al. (2012) studied 6 consanguineous Bruck syndrome families. They also described a patient with autosomal recessive osteogenesis imperfecta, and 2 brothers, one affected with mild autosomal recessive osteogenesis imperfecta and the other with mild Bruck syndrome, all with PLOD2 mutations (see MOLECULAR GENETICS), indicating that PLOD2 mutations cause connective tissue disorders within a Bruck syndrome-osteogenesis imperfecta phenotypic spectrum.

paragraphs.text: The transmission pattern of Bruck syndrome-2 is consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance. Ha-Vinh et al. (2004) found a homozygous PLOD2 mutation in an affected boy, and Puig-Hervas et al. (2012) found homozygous or compound heterozygous PLOD2 mutations in patients from consanguineous families.

paragraphs.text: Bank et al. (1999) studied a family with Bruck syndrome in which lysine residues within the telopeptides of type I collagen in bone were underhydroxylated, leading to aberrant crosslinking, whereas cartilage and ligament showed normal crosslinking. A genome screen identified only a single region, on chromosome 17p12, where all affected sibs shared a cluster of haplotypes identical by descent, suggesting that this region might contain the Bruck syndrome locus (see BRKS1).

checks.explanation: The reference to affected sibs implies a single family with Bruck syndrome. The abstract does not use the word 'family' or say how many families were studied.

paragraphs.text: In 6 consanguineous families with Bruck syndrome, Puig-Hervas et al. (2012) detected mutations in either PLOD2 or FKBP10 in all cases. Two probands had a homozygous frameshift mutation in the alternative exon 13a of PLOD2, indicating that specific inactivation of the longer protein isoform encoded by the gene is sufficient to cause Bruck syndrome. By homozygosity mapping followed by a candidate gene approach, they also identified a homozygous donor splice site mutation in PLOD2 in a patient with autosomal recessive osteogenesis imperfecta. Screening of additional samples revealed compound heterozygous PLOD2 mutations in 2 brothers, one affected with mild autosomal recessive osteogenesis imperfecta and the other with mild Bruck syndrome.
